content: 1. Etonogestrel/ethinyl estradiol is indicated for use in females of reproductive age. A single NuvaRing is inserted into the vagina and remains in place for three weeks. After three weeks, the ring is removed for a one-week break, during which withdrawal bleeding typically occurs. A new ring should then be inserted one week after the previous ring was removed. Refer to administration guidelines for specific instructions on ring insertion timing. 2. Ethinyl estradiol increases the level or effect of fezolinetant by altering hepatic enzyme CYP1A2 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. Co-administration with weak, moderate, or strong CYP1A2 inhibitors increases fezolinetant AUC and peak plasma concentration. 3. Ethinyl estradiol, when co-administered with ombitasvir/paritaprevir/ritonavir and dasabuvir, can lead to significant ALT elevations (>5x ULN, including some >20x ULN). Ethinyl estradiol-containing medications should be discontinued before initiating this hepatitis C combination regimen and restarted approximately two weeks after completing the regimen. 4. Co-administration of tranexamic acid and ethinyl estradiol increases the risk of thrombosis due to pharmacodynamic synergism. This combination is contraindicated. 5. Amobarbital decreases the level or effect of ethinyl estradiol by inducing hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Hormonal contraceptive efficacy may be reduced; nonhormonal contraceptive methods are recommended. 6. Ethinyl estradiol reduces the efficacy of anastrozole through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Anastrozole should not be used concurrently with estrogens or estrogen-containing products. 7. Apalutamide decreases the level or effect of ethinyl estradiol by inducing hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Hormonal contraceptive efficacy may be reduced; nonhormonal contraceptive methods are recommended. 8. Armodafinil decreases the level or effect of ethinyl estradiol by inducing hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Hormonal contraceptive efficacy may be reduced; nonhormonal contraceptive methods are recommended. 9. Atazanavir may cause significant changes in estrogen plasma levels when co-administered with ethinyl estradiol. Hormonal contraceptive efficacy may be reduced; nonhormonal contraceptive methods are recommended. 10. Belzutifan decreases the level or effect of ethinyl estradiol by inducing hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Hormonal contraceptive failure or increased breakthrough bleeding may occur. Nonhormonal contraceptive methods are recommended due to potential fetal harm based on animal studies. 11. Bosentan decreases the level or effect of ethinyl estradiol by inducing hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Hormonal contraceptive efficacy may be reduced; nonhormonal contraceptive methods are recommended. 12. Brigatinib decreases the level or effect of ethinyl estradiol and etonogestrel by inducing hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Hormonal contraceptive efficacy may be reduced, and fetal harm is possible. Women should use effective nonhormonal contraception during treatment and for at least four months after the last dose. 13. Butabarbital decreases the level or effect of ethinyl estradiol by inducing hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Hormonal contraceptive efficacy may be reduced; nonhormonal contraceptive methods are recommended. 14. Carbamazepine decreases the level or effect of etonogestrel and ethinyl estradiol by inducing hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Hormonal contraceptive efficacy may be reduced; nonhormonal contraceptive methods are recommended. 15. Calaspargase pegol may indirectly interact with oral contraceptives, reducing their efficacy. Non-oral contraceptive methods are recommended for females of childbearing potential. 16. Clarithromycin increases the level or effect of etonogestrel by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Alternative drugs should be considered. 17. Conivaptan increases the level or effect of ethinyl estradiol by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Alternative drugs should be considered. 18. Dexamethasone decreases the level or effect of ethinyl estradiol by inducing hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Hormonal contraceptive efficacy may be reduced; nonhormonal contraceptive methods are recommended. 19. Efavirenz decreases the level or effect of ethinyl estradiol by inducing hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Hormonal contraceptive efficacy may be reduced; nonhormonal contraceptive methods are recommended. 20. Ethinyl estradiol reduces the efficacy of elagolix through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Nonhormonal contraceptive methods are recommended during treatment and for one week after discontinuation. 21. Elvitegravir decreases the level or effect of ethinyl estradiol by an unknown mechanism. Nonhormonal contraceptive methods are recommended. 22. Enasidenib increases the level or effect of ethinyl estradiol by inhibiting specific transport proteins. Co-administration with sensitive substrates should be avoided or adjusted. 23. Encorafenib decreases the level or effect of ethinyl estradiol by inducing hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Hormonal contraceptive efficacy may be reduced, and fetal harm is possible. Nonhormonal contraceptive methods are recommended during treatment and for two weeks after the final dose. 24. Ethinyl estradiol reduces the efficacy of enoxaparin through pharmacodynamic antagonism. This combination is contraindicated due to the risk of thromboembolic disorders. 25. Enzalutamide decreases the level or effect of ethinyl estradiol by inducing hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Hormonal contraceptive efficacy may be reduced; nonhormonal contraceptive methods are recommended. 26. Erythromycin (base, ethylsuccinate, lactobionate, stearate) increases the level or effect of etonogestrel by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Alternative drugs should be considered. 27. Eslicarbazepine acetate decreases the level or effect of ethinyl estradiol by inducing hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Nonhormonal contraceptive methods are recommended. 28. Ethinyl estradiol reduces the efficacy of exemestane through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Exemestane should not be used concurrently with estrogens or estrogen-containing products. 29. Ethinyl estradiol increases the level or effect of fedratinib by inhibiting specific enzymes. Co-administration with dual CYP3A4 and CYP2C19 inhibitors should be avoided. 30. Fexinidazole increases the level or effect of ethinyl estradiol by inhibiting hepatic enzyme CYP2E1 metabolism. Co-administration may increase the risk of adverse effects. 31. Fosamprenavir may alter hormone levels when co-administered with ethinyl estradiol. Nonhormonal contraceptive methods are recommended. 32. Griseofulvin decreases the level or effect of ethinyl estradiol by inducing hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Hormonal contraceptive efficacy may be reduced; nonhormonal contraceptive methods are recommended. 33. Ethinyl estradiol reduces the efficacy of heparin through pharmacodynamic antagonism. This combination is contraindicated due to the risk of thromboembolic disorders. 34. Idelalisib increases the level or effect of ethinyl estradiol by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration with sensitive substrates should be avoided. 35. Indinavir may cause significant changes in estrogen plasma levels when co-administered with ethinyl estradiol. Hormonal contraceptive efficacy may be reduced; nonhormonal contraceptive methods are recommended. 36. Isavuconazonium sulfate increases the level or effect of ethinyl estradiol by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Alternative drugs should be considered. 37. Ivosidenib decreases the level or effect of ethinyl estradiol by inducing hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration with sensitive substrates should be avoided. 38. Leniolisib increases the level or effect of ethinyl estradiol by inhibiting specific transport proteins. Nonhormonal contraceptive methods are recommended. 39. Lesinurad decreases the level or effect of etonogestrel by inducing hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Nonhormonal contraceptive methods are recommended. 40. Ethinyl estradiol reduces the efficacy of letrozole through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Letrozole should not be used concurrently with estrogens or estrogen-containing products. 41. Lumacaftor/ivacaftor decreases the level or effect of etonogestrel and ethinyl estradiol by an unspecified mechanism. Hormonal contraceptive efficacy may be reduced; nonhormonal contraceptive methods are recommended. 42. Ethinyl estradiol increases the level or effect of lonafarnib by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration with weak inhibitors should be closely monitored. 43. Lopinavir may cause significant changes in estrogen plasma levels when co-administered with ethinyl estradiol. Hormonal contraceptive efficacy may be reduced; nonhormonal contraceptive methods are recommended. 44. Mavacamten decreases the level or effect of etonogestrel by inducing hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Nonhormonal contraceptive methods are recommended.
